promise: The agent's natural output is the cockpit itself — panels are to Vysted what files are to a code editor.
evidence: src/lib/host-actions.ts applyHostAction (:880-1400) resolves every agent action to a workspace-store panel open/arrange call (ws.openPanel/openCompanyOverview/loadSymbolIntoChart) rather than returning chat-only text; ChatSidebar.tsx:357-359 states panels are the agent's output surface.

promise: Two users are first-class in one workspace, never two apps: the agent-delegator (novice) and the hands-on driver (finance-literate user).
evidence: src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:356 "four-mode spine (Ask / Edit / Build / Delegate)" running in the SAME workspace store as manual panel drag/drop (src/components/PanelHost.tsx dockview host); no separate app/window for either path — both read/write useWorkspaceStore.
gap: Terminology drifted from the constitution's literal 'agent-delegator / hands-on driver' framing to the mode-spine framing (Ask/Edit/Build/Delegate) — same mechanism, different label; not a functional gap.

promise: Every capability MUST be reachable both by hand and by agent.
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py Capability dataclass (:79-90) — every agent-reachable capability declares a `kind` (read_handler/host_action/mcp_endpoint) that also drives a UI-reachable route/panel; the READ_ONLY host-action set in src/lib/host-actions.ts mirrors the same catalog ids the agent calls, so the same action is reachable by clicking the panel or by the agent invoking the tool.

promise: The switch between leaning on the agent and driving by hand MUST be a single, non-destructive gesture.
evidence: No lock/disable gate on panels while an agent run streams was found (grepped src/components/PanelHost.tsx and src/modules/*/*.tsx for a streaming-disables-panel pattern — none exists); dockview panels stay live and directly editable during a streaming agent run, so switching to hands-on is just clicking the panel, and the composer's stop control (ChatSidebar.tsx onDone/fail handlers, :913-921) ends a run without tearing down any panel state.
gap: No single NAMED control literally toggles 'mode' — the non-destructive switch is implicit (panels are simply always interactive), not a documented, discoverable affordance a new user would find.

promise: The agent does the ambiguous upfront work, then hands off to the manipulable cockpit — it never traps a user inside a chat transcript for work that wants direct manipulation.
evidence: src/lib/host-actions.ts applyHostAction opens/arranges panels (openPanel/openCompanyOverview/loadSymbolIntoChart, e.g. :935,:1116,:1169,:1349) rather than rendering data as more chat text — every substantial output hands off to a panel the user can then directly manipulate.

promise: Every terminal capability (quotes, charts, screener, fundamentals, portfolio, news, quant, brokers, …) is defined once in a single capability catalog and projected to all consumers (built-in copilot/personas AND external MCP clients).
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py — the Capability dataclass (:79-92) is the single declaration; TOOL_SCHEMAS (schemas.py) and mcp_capabilities() (catalog.py:1496) both project from the SAME `CAPABILITIES` registry (per CLAUDE.md's documented derivation and test_capability_catalog.py / test_mcp_catalog_parity.py which audit registry<->catalog and internal<->MCP parity).

promise: The internal agent adapter and the external MCP adapter are two renderers of the same source of truth, not two hand-maintained surfaces.
evidence: sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:141-153 builds each MCP tool's `readOnlyHint` directly from the SAME `capability.read_only` flag the internal copilot adapter reads off the same Capability object — one declaration, two renderers, not two hand-maintained lists.

promise: A capability MUST NOT exist for only one consumer.
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py mcp_capabilities() (:1496) filters/derives from the same CAPABILITIES list every internal TOOL_SCHEMAS entry comes from — there is no separate 'MCP-only' or 'internal-only' capability table (hand-written MCP-only tools like agent/workspace/workflow ops are the documented exception, not a violation of the single-catalog rule for terminal DATA capabilities).

promise: One read_only declaration drives both the internal mutation gate and the external readOnlyHint.
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py Capability.read_only (:88) is read both by the internal tool-schema gate (schemas.py TOOL_SCHEMAS derivation) and by mcp_server.py:153 readOnlyHint=capability.read_only — same field, both surfaces.

promise: Vysted is a framework people build finance agents and trade-bots on, not a closed app.
evidence: docs/MCP_INTEGRATION.md:1-16 — "Vysted-as-server": the sidecar mounts a FastMCP app at /mcp; external clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code) consume Vysted's data + agent surface as MCP tools; plugins/ (openbb-mcp, brokers, vysted-lenses, vysted-news) + types/plugin.ts's `agent-collection`/`trading-bot` PluginType (types/plugin.ts:28) let a third party ship its own agents/bots on top.

promise: Read-only is the default; every mutation is explicit, gated, and audited.
evidence: sidecar/services/broker_base.py — read-only wrapper base class gates every mutating path behind kill-switch + confirm-time re-check (:246-346); Capability.read_only (catalog.py:88) makes the default explicit per-tool; audit_log.py enforces every actual mutation lands in the append-only trail (see INT-SP-14/35).

promise: The append-only audit log is enforced at the database level (SQLite triggers + a read-only reader connection), not by convention.
evidence: sidecar/models/audit_log.py AUDIT_LOG_DDL — BEFORE UPDATE (line 41) and BEFORE DELETE (line 47) triggers RAISE(ABORT) on audit_orders (per CLAUDE.md's documented sqlite3.IntegrityError behaviour); the reader connection is opened PRAGMA query_only=ON per the same file's documented pattern.

promise: Type-gated execution: mutations are only reachable through an explicit confirm path, plus a grep-time audit over all call sites.
evidence: sidecar/tests/test_safety_end_to_end.py — a dedicated §6.5 8-point audit suite; test_audit_1_paper_mode_default (:119) and test_audit_2_no_bypass_path_to_place_confirmed (:163-178) literally `subprocess.run(["grep", ...])` over the broker call sites and assert no live-mode / no-bypass literal exists, i.e. the grep-time audit runs as an executed test, not a manual review step.

promise: A kill-switch halts the mutating path.
evidence: sidecar/services/broker_base.py:251-252 (`if kill_switch.get_bus().is_fired: raise BrokerError(...halted...)`) at propose time AND :345-346 re-checked at confirm time ("Kill switch may have fired in" the gap between propose and confirm); src-tauri/src/kill_switch.rs:34-94 wires the Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K global shortcut to emit the same event the Python bus subscribes to.

promise: Read-only-by-default wrappers: no mutating methods on a provider's public surface; GET-only routers; supportsControlPlane = false.

promise: Every agent-proposed change (panel config, portfolio, workspace build, and especially orders) renders as a reviewable preview→applied diff (accept-all/reject-all/per-item, keyboard-driven).
evidence: src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:358-359 — "every agent-proposed mutation is staged as a reviewable diff (FR-010) — nothing lands before the user accepts"; useProposedChangesStore referenced at :928-931 gates a pending publish_brief the same way; portfolio/workspace mutations route through the same proposed-changes store per host-actions.ts (:1349,:1373,:1387 openPanel("portfolio") after a staged change, not a direct write).

promise: Orders never auto-apply; there is no 'YOLO' path.
evidence: src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:359-360 — "Orders route through the §6.5 dialog (FR-011); the AI never reaches placement."; sidecar/services/broker_base.py's propose/confirm split (kill-switch re-checked at BOTH steps, :246-346) structurally prevents a single agent call from both proposing and executing an order.

promise: Autonomous agent runs are bounded by a hard ceiling on tokens/spend/wall-clock/steps (a BudgetGuard).
evidence: sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:1-90 — BudgetGuard accumulates tokens/spend_usd/wall_seconds/steps and reports the FIRST breached ceiling (SC-008, docstring :1-8); sidecar/services/run_manager.py:53,103-110 wires BudgetGuard into every Delegate/background run via on_round_usage.
gap: BudgetGuard only wraps DETACHED Delegate runs (run_manager.py). The foreground interactive chat loop (sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:539-543 _MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS=6) caps rounds/steps but has no token/spend/wall-clock ceiling of its own — acceptable since 'autonomous agent runs' in the constitution maps to the background/Delegate surface, not the supervised foreground chat, but worth flagging if the promise is read to cover both.

promise: Vysted runs fully on the user's machine with no hosted backend.
evidence: README.md:3-5 — "No account, no hosted backend, no telemetry: data and secrets stay on your machine."; sidecar/main.py:101 binds --host default 127.0.0.1; README.md:22-25 describes the three-process, loopback-only architecture (Rust core + Next.js static export + Python sidecar).

promise: All provider and model keys are operator-supplied.
evidence: README.md:29 "BYOK across 7 LLM providers"; src-tauri/src/keychain.rs SERVICE="vysted-terminal" (:36) is the only place a provider secret is written, always via a renderer-side settings action, never bundled/hard-coded.

promise: Secrets live in the OS keychain; the renderer reads them and passes them per request; the sidecar cannot read the keychain.
evidence: src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:1-30 module doc + keychain_get/keychain_set (:299-332) — the renderer/Rust core owns the OS keychain (keyring::Entry, :65-85); the Python sidecar has no keychain-reading code path (grepped sidecar/ for `keyring` import — none), matching "the sidecar cannot read the keychain."

promise: Secrets are least-privilege at point of use, never logged, echoed, or persisted beyond process memory.
evidence: src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:1-2 module doc "never on disk in the browser, never in plaintext logs"; secrets cross to the sidecar only as a per-request header per CLAUDE.md's documented BYOK pattern, never persisted server-side.

promise: The sidecar binds loopback only.
evidence: sidecar/main.py:101 `parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1", ...)`; src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:96 and sec_edgar_mcp.rs:96 both hard-set their subprocess host env var to 127.0.0.1 as well.

promise: No user data leaves the machine unless a plugin explicitly routes it outward, and that routing is visible.
evidence: types/plugin.ts DataSource/PluginCapabilities contract has no implicit network-egress path; any outward routing is a plugin's own declared behaviour (contributesData sources are explicit, named, and shown in the plugin manager per CLAUDE.md's plugin-contract section) rather than a hidden host-level telemetry call.
gap: No dedicated 'egress visibility' UI/audit (e.g. a per-plugin network-call log) was found in this sweep beyond the plugin manager's declared-sources list — this is closer to 'egress is opt-in and declared' than 'every outbound call is visibly logged'; would need a data-egress raw finding if a plugin's contributesData source silently calls out without appearing in that list, which this pass did not test.

promise: Credential storage MUST NOT regress to plaintext files or machine-ID-derived encryption.
evidence: src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:1-30 — RELEASE builds (`cfg(not(debug_assertions))`) use ONLY the OS keychain (os_keychain module, :62-86); the plaintext `dev-keystore.json` file backend is compiled ONLY under `cfg(debug_assertions)` and is asserted absent from release by `release_never_uses_dev_keystore` (module doc :19-21). The dev keystore itself is COMMON.md out-of-scope ("reopening ... the dev keystore") and not machine-ID-derived (it is a build-time dev convenience, not an at-rest encryption scheme).
decision_ref: COMMON.md out-of-scope-by-decision list — dev keystore reopening excluded

promise: The plugin contract stays serializable (no framework types cross it).

This contract uses `unknown` instead"; PanelSpec.component (:113-117) is a string id resolved by the host at mount time specifically so "the contract stays serializable and free of framework types."

promise: The platform — not the agent roster or the license — is the durable moat.

promise: Every data response carries provenance (which provider served it).
evidence: sidecar/models/market.py Quote.provider: str (:23) and OHLCVSeries.provider: str (:44-46, non-optional) — every market-data model carries a mandatory provider field; types/data.ts:151,170 mirror per-field provenance/coverage metadata for fundamentals (R13).

promise: Every agent claim that asserts a fact carries citations.
evidence: types/brief.ts:6,309-312 — the research-brief contract carries markdown with `[n]` citation markers backed by a `sources: BriefSource[]` array with real URLs (:232); BriefStructuredLeg (:22-36) tags every data leg with `provider`. This machinery covers the DEEP/FAST research and brief-publish path.
gap: A plain chat-turn factual claim made OUTSIDE the research/brief pipeline (e.g. the model states a number from a tool result inline in normal chat prose) has no code-enforced citation object — citation enforcement rides the brief contract, not every assistant turn that asserts a fact, so it is not true for 'every agent claim' as literally stated.

promise: Every mutation lands in the append-only audit trail.
evidence: sidecar/models/audit_log.py AUDIT_LOG_DDL append-only triggers (:41,:47) plus sidecar/services/broker_base.py's mutation gate (kill-switch + confirm-time re-check, :246-346) sit directly in front of the only mutating call path, so every mutation that reaches execution necessarily passes through the audited path.

promise: The provider/model/cost in use is always legible on the agent surface.
evidence: Provider/model ARE legible: src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:398,439,507,767-782 — an explicit HUD provider/model override resolved every send. But src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:921 `updateRun(runId, { cost: { tokens: usage.inputTokens + usage.outputTokens, spendUsd: 0, steps: 0 } })` hard-codes spendUsd to literal 0 for every foreground run regardless of the model/provider actually used or its real per-token price.
gap: Cost is NOT legible on the agent surface for foreground runs — every run's spend reads $0.00 in the run history/HUD no matter what was actually spent, which directly contradicts 'the provider/model/cost in use is always legible.' (BudgetGuard computes a real spend_usd estimate for Delegate/background runs only — run_manager.py:103-110 — so the gap is specific to the foreground chat path.)

promise: Trust is earned with verifiable artifacts, not asserted — and never simulated (no fabricated data behind a 'populated' surface).

gap: The verifiable-artifact mechanism (source-matching + citation tray) exists on the Equity Overview narrative and the research Brief specifically, not as a blanket cross-cutting layer over every surface that could show a model-written number (e.g. a plain chat answer with no brief/narrative wrapper has no equivalent unverified-figure check).
